title: String reproduction through an offset-addressed retrieval service
summary: A string is deposited symbol by symbol. After the separator a retrieval service returns, in one step, the deposited symbol at the current offset, for any offset. Pairs and brackets use the same service with other addresses.
core_idea: Reproduce strings by one-step retrieval of the symbol deposited at each offset.

state.name: Dp
state.meaning: Deposit area of C symbols, C = 64.

state.name: Svc
state.meaning: Retrieval service: Svc(a) returns the symbol deposited at address a in one step.

state.name: Em2
state.meaning: Learned map from retrieved symbol to output.

update.latex: t < t_{sep}: Dp_{nd} \leftarrow x_t,\; nd \leftarrow nd + 1;\quad t > t_{sep}: off \leftarrow off + 1
update.plain: symbols are deposited until the separator step t_sep; then the offset counts emitted symbols
update.name: deposit

readout.plain: the service returns the symbol at the offset and Em2 maps it; for pairs the address is the probe symbol, for brackets the depth

learning.description: Em2 by majority over the m items; the address source is chosen by training accuracy.
learning.few_shot_argument: Em2 is the identity on D = 4 symbols; m = 4 strings of length 64 cover them.

complexity.constants_notes: One deposit or one service call per token; C + 3 words.

sample_efficiency.mechanism: Service reads leave only Em2 to learn.

prediction.statement: From m = 4 strings of length 64 over D = 4, per-symbol accuracy of the copy is at least 0.99.

capabilities.prediction: Strings longer than C = 64 cannot be reproduced exactly: L = 65 over D = 4 is 130 bits against 128 bits of deposit.

known_relatives.name: not assessed
known_relatives.relation: This card does not compare its mechanism with others.
known_relatives.claimed_difference: No difference from earlier work is claimed.

falsifiers: Counted operations per token that grow with C.
4 strings of length 64 after which copy accuracy is below 0.99.

toy_example.description: Deposit four symbols and retrieve them by offset.
toy_example.python:
import json
src = [2, 0, 3, 1]
Dp = list(src)
print(json.dumps({"copy": [Dp[o] for o in range(4)], "same": [Dp[o] for o in range(4)] == src}))
